newsitem.title: USA: US spot prods up late day, Phillips plant up Thurs.
newsitem.headline: US spot prods up late day, Phillips plant up Thurs.

text.p: U.S. spot product prices stood higher late Thursday afternoon, partly on talk Phillips Petroleum had problems with restarting a catalytic cracker at its Sweeny, Texas refinery, traders said.

Phillips said late Thursday afternoon it planned to restore the 64,000 barrel per day cracker to service by later this evening, ending any bullish trade connected to talk of a delay in doing so following maintenance.
Gasoline markets on the U.S. Gulf Coast, quite thin before the Phillips talk spilled into the market, firmed a touch, as did NYMEX futures markets, traders said.

Gulf Coast "M1" unleaded gasoline diffs firmed 0.40 cent a gallon to 2.85 cents below May futures for front eleventh cycle material on reports the refinery had to delay restarting a 87,000 barrel per day cracker down for maintenance over the past two months.

New York "M2" grade, meanwhile, was heard done at 4.00 cents below the May print, almost 1.50 cents weaker than Wednesday. But that deal was dismissed by some players, who said it was related to a distressed cargo in NYH.
They said the market was more likely around 3.00 cents under, still about 0.50 cent under May futures.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk, 1 212 859 1633
